narrative.intro: Granite Construction has $562M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company won 11 awards so far, with an average award size of $51.1M, and obligations are up 133.9% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security accounts for most federal spending with $537M in obligations. Other federal buyers include the Department of Defense with $13.4M and the Department of Transportation with $11.7M. On the industry side, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction represents $537M of obligations, while Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction represent $13.1M and $11.8M respectively. Smaller federal work includes Asphalt Paving Mixture and Block Manufacturing at $250K. Past fiscal years show a ramp-up in federal work: FY21 obligations were $20.3M, FY22 were $19.7M, FY23 were $335M, FY24 were $185M, and FY25 were $240M. This profile shows concentrated spending with a single agency and a few construction-related markets driving the FY2026 totals.

sections.heading: Who are Granite Construction's top federal buyers?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security is the top buyer, obligating $537M to Granite Construction in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense obligated $13.4M and the Department of Transportation obligated $11.7M. Together these agencies make up the principal sources of the FY2026 obligations.

sections.heading: What federal markets and contract sizes does Granite Construction serve?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market with $537M in obligations. Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction accounts for $13.1M, Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction accounts for $11.8M, and Asphalt Paving Mixture and Block Manufacturing accounts for $250K. The average award size in FY2026 to date is $51.1M across 11 awards.

faq.q: How much does Granite Construction make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Granite Construction has received $562M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company won 11 awards with an average award size of $51.1M, and obligations are up 133.9% year over year. Fiscal-year history shows FY21 at $20.3M, FY22 at $19.7M, FY23 at $335M, FY24 at $185M, and FY25 at $240M.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Granite Construction?
faq.a: The Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Transportation are the main buyers. The Department of Homeland Security obligated $537M, the Department of Defense obligated $13.4M, and the Department of Transportation obligated $11.7M in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: What does Granite Construction sell to the government?
faq.a: Granite Construction sells construction and paving work to the government. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction accounts for $537M, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction accounts for $13.1M, Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction accounts for $11.8M, and Asphalt Paving Mixture and Block Manufacturing accounts for $250K.

faq.q: Which Granite Construction contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: No Granite Construction contracts are listed as expiring soon in the FY2026 to date figures. The available FY2026 to date record does not include expiring-contract entries.
